figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section of a plant stem or leaf part, stained blue-green and magenta. A single-layered epidermis lies along the top, with small thick-walled cells beneath it. Below that are several vascular bundles with magenta-stained thick-walled cells, set in large, thin-walled, rounded cells with air spaces. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section of a Ranunculus root, stained blue. A small central stele with xylem and surrounding tissue is ringed by a wide cortex of rounded parenchyma cells. The cortex has several large irregular air spaces, and an outer epidermis forms the edge. No labels are printed on the image.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through part of a leaf, stained blue-green. A thin lamina with palisade cells, spongy mesophyll with air spaces and an epidermis on each surface leads to a large rounded midrib that bulges out below. The midrib has a central vascular bundle with xylem and phloem, surrounded by large parenchyma cells. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section of a plant root, stained blue and purple. At the centre is a star-shaped xylem with five arms. It is made of large, empty, thick-walled cells with dark purple walls. Patches of smaller phloem cells lie between the arms, surrounded by a ring of small cells. Larger rounded cortex cells with purple-speckled contents surround this central region. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two potted plants of the same type with dark green, lobed, palmate leaves. The plant on the left is in a green pot and has upright stems with firm, spread leaves. The plant on the right is in a red-brown pot and has drooping, limp stems and leaves that hang over the pot edge, as if wilted. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light microscope view of a leaf epidermal peel with large epidermal cells that have wavy, interlocking walls. Two stomata are visible, one at the top centre and one at the bottom left. Each stoma is an oval pair of guard cells surrounding a central slit-like pore. No labels, scale or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A coloured scanning electron micrograph of part of a transverse section through a rolled xerophytic leaf. The leaf is folded into deep pits and grooves, and long hairs project from the surface into the pits. Cells with large air spaces are visible inside the leaf. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of a leaf surface in which two sunken pits (stomatal openings) show green interior surfaces, with grey-white textured tissue surrounding and covering most of the surface. It has no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) with flat, green, pad-like stems grows from sandy, dry ground with tufts of dry grass. A spiky agave-like plant is at the lower left. Behind it is a dry, rocky valley with a river and mountains under a cloudy sky. There are no labels.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A grey scanning electron micrograph of a dense mat of star-shaped, branching hairs with long thin spines radiating from central points. The hairs overlap and interlock across the surface, with a rough surface visible at the bottom left. No labels, scale bar or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A colour photograph of a dense clump of succulent cactus-like plants with thick, green, ribbed, upright and curving fleshy stems and no visible leaves. They grow on dry, rocky ground on a hillside with sparse dry vegetation. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section of plant tissue (marram grass leaf) stained blue and pink. There is a large elongated cavity or groove lined with blue-stained cells, and surrounding rounded cells with thickened blue walls. A vascular bundle with a ring of blue-stained cells sits at the top. No labels or values are printed.
figures.original: It is useful to observe the xerophytic features of marram grass (Figure 7.21a) for yourself by examining a transverse section with a light microscope and making an annotated drawing using Figure 7.22 to he

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained transverse section of a rolled marram grass leaf seen under a light microscope. The leaf is curled into a near-circle with a gap at the top. The inner surface has deep folds and ridges with pink-purple hairs projecting into the central hollow space. Blue-stained tissue contains small vascular bundles, and the outer edge has a layer of cells. No labels are printed.
figures.original: It is useful to observe the xerophytic features of marram grass (Figure 7.21a) for yourself by examining a transverse section with a light microscope and making an annotated drawing using Figure 7.22 to he

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section of plant xylem tissue. Several large, round, empty vessels with thick walls stained red are surrounded by many smaller, angular cells, also with red-stained walls. No labels, scale bar or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A line drawing of a plant tissue in transverse section, with no labels. It has large rounded thick-walled cells with pits (short double lines across the walls), and small thin-walled cells of varying size at the bottom. Several angular cells between the large cells are filled with stippling.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A line drawing of a plant tissue in cross-section. It has several large, thick-walled, empty round or oval cells, which look like xylem vessels. Between them are smaller thick-walled cells and areas of dense stipple. There are no labels or values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a longitudinal section of plant xylem, stained blue-green with red-orange lignified thickening. The wide vessel on the left has closely spaced ladder-like (scalariform) thickening bars. The narrower vessels to the right have spiral or annular thickening. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A colour-enhanced scanning electron micrograph of xylem vessels cut open. The vessels are wide hollow tubes with orange walls that have closely spaced ridges, like rings, on the inside. They are surrounded by pale green tissue. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a single pale, thin plant root lying vertically among soil particles of sand grains and dark crumbs. Many fine, hair-like outgrowths (root hairs) stick out from the sides of the root along most of its length. The root tip is at the bottom. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a stained plant tissue in transverse section, with many small, thick-walled, roughly polygonal cells. The cell walls are stained blue and the cell contents are mostly empty and white. Cell sizes vary, with smaller cells at the left and lower areas and larger cells toward the centre and right. A dark stained patch of crushed cells lies in the upper left of centre. No labels or scale are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a longitudinal section of plant tissue, stained green and yellow. Long, narrow cells run vertically, and on the right side there are larger, rounder cells. Two elongated tubes have dark red-brown blobs at their ends, which look like sieve plates with callose. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A gloved hand holds a metal, flat, heart-shaped artificial pump device with two ribbed, flexible white tubes rising from its top. One tube has a purple ring and the other a blue ring at the metal connector. Arrows on the connectors point up on the left and down on the right. Clear plastic tubing is on the left, and surgeons in green gowns and masks stand in an operating theatre in the background.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through an artery (left) and a vein (right) lying side by side in surrounding connective tissue. The artery has a thick, dark purple muscular wall around a small round empty lumen. The vein has a thinner wall and a larger, irregular, oval lumen that contains pale pink material. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained light micrograph of tissue in which a row of dark magenta-purple, roughly square cells lies along a diagonal line from upper left to lower right. Pale, clear spaces lie between the cells. The surrounding tissue is blue-purple and fibrous, with a few pink-purple oval structures scattered around it. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of blood. Several large red biconcave discs (red blood cells) are shown. One rounded blue cell with a surface covered in small projections (a white blood cell) sits left of centre. Many small yellow-green irregular spiky fragments (platelets) lie among them. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained blood smear viewed under a microscope. Many pink-red red blood cells surround three white blood cells in the centre. On the left is a cell with a lobed, dark purple nucleus and pale cytoplasm. In the middle is a small, round, dark purple cell. On the right is a larger cell with a mottled purple nucleus. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of a single cell with a surface covered in small projections (microvilli). The cell appears cut open: the interior cytoplasm is coloured blue and a large irregular nucleus is coloured green. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A drawing of cardiac muscle fibres, pink-purple and branching, with striations and oval blue-purple nuclei. Dark purple zigzag lines mark the junctions between fibres (intercalated discs). White gaps between the fibres are labelled as containing connective tissue and blood capillaries. A bracket marks the width of one cardiac muscle fibre.
labels: space between fibres, containing connective tissue and blood capillaries

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a whole heart, pink and seen against a black background. The coronary blood vessels are dark red and branch across the surface; the main vessel curves across the top and down the right side, and many smaller branches spread through the tissue. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of the inside of a heart ventricle that has been cut open. It shows the thick red muscular wall, the pale tendon-like cords (heart strings) and papillary muscles, and ridged muscle on the inner surface. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A grey-scale light micrograph of a transverse section through two blood vessels lying side by side in surrounding tissue. The vessel on the right is round with a thick, dark wall and a small circular lumen. The vessel on the left is larger and irregular with a thin wall and a wide, empty lumen. The question text refers to labels X and Y, but no labels are visible on the image.
figures.original: The micrograph shows an artery and a vein. Which row correctly identifies and describes the artery and the vein? X Y Description A artery vein The artery has thick walls and the vein has thin w

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An endoscopic view inside the airways at the point where the trachea divides into the two main bronchi. Two dark openings are visible, left and right, with ridged walls from the cartilage rings. The lining is pink to red, and a whitish or pale patch sits on the ridge between the openings and extends down toward the bottom of the image. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An unlabelled drawing of a small airway branching into two smaller tubes, each ending in a cluster of rounded, bubble-like sacs. This is a group of alveoli at the end of a bronchiole. It has no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a stained section through the wall of the trachea. At the top is a band of pink-red tissue containing glands and small blue-ringed cells, with a thin ridged lining along the upper edge. Below it is a broad pale orange layer of cartilage with many blue-stained cells (chondrocytes) scattered through it. There are no labels or scale bar.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a cross-section of a small airway in lung tissue, stained pink and purple. The airway wall is folded into many finger-like projections lined with a darker purple epithelium around a central open lumen. Thin alveolar tissue with air spaces surrounds the airway. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained light micrograph of part of an airway wall. Folded epithelium with pink-stained cells and dark nuclei lies on the left, with a band of smooth muscle beside it. A large pink plate of cartilage containing small cells in spaces (lacunae) lies on the right. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of the airway lining. Tufts of yellow cilia stand out from red-brown cells that are covered in short microvilli. A single rounded red cell with yellow speckles lies at the bottom right. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour micrograph of a section through a bronchiole wall. The tissue is magenta and yellow-green, with dark red blood cells inside the vessels, against a blue background. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a stained section of lung tissue. It shows many thin-walled air spaces (alveoli) with pink-red stained walls and red blood cells in the capillaries. At the bottom is a bronchiole with a folded lining of epithelium and a surrounding wall of tissue with darkly stained nuclei. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour CT scan of a cross-section through the chest. The image has no labels. The right lung on the image is black with a small amount of coloured tissue, and the left lung on the image is mottled with orange, green, blue and red patches. A large orange area in the centre is the heart and mediastinum, and the spine is at the bottom centre. The ribs and chest wall form a ring around the lungs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of lung tissue stained pink-red, as seen in emphysema. It shows several large, irregular, empty air spaces separated by thin, ragged alveolar walls. Black specks of carbon or dust are scattered in the walls. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A colored scanning electron micrograph of the surface of the airway lining. Dense tufts of fine, hair-like cilia cover the left and upper parts. On the right and lower parts are smooth, rounded, brown cells without cilia, which are bulging and look like goblet cells or cells that have lost their cilia. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of lung tissue stained purple/pink on a pale blue-green background. It shows large, empty air spaces (alveoli) separated by very thin walls, with thicker clusters of stained tissue at the edges. There are no labels or scale values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of lung tissue stained pink and purple. It shows several large, air-filled alveolar spaces separated by very thin walls. Small dark purple nuclei lie along the walls, with a few small capillaries containing cells. No labels or scale are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of the head of a mosquito seen from the front and side. It shows two large compound eyes made of many round lenses, coloured purple and orange-red, with hairy antennae, mouthparts with a forked tip, and a wing at the upper right, all against a black background. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour micrograph of a single rod-shaped bacterium on a dark background. The cell is coloured red and green and has one long, wavy, thin flagellum extending from one end down to the bottom left. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained blood smear viewed under a microscope. It shows many pale brown-red red blood cells on a pale yellow background. Several cells contain small purple-blue ring-shaped parasites with dark dots, consistent with Plasmodium at the ring stage. One cell at the lower right has a ring with a red-purple spot. One cell in the centre holds two or three rings. No labels or scale are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour micrograph of a cross-section through a structure with a ring of eight rounded compartments around a ninth central one. Each compartment holds a green-yellow centre surrounded by purple, blue and orange material, and some contain small black dots. The compartments are separated by white spaces inside a grainy blue outer layer. No labels or scale are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour electron micrograph of a dividing rod-shaped bacterial cell cut in section, on a black background. The cell is yellow with a brown outer wall and a constriction forming where it is dividing. It has several blue patches inside, which are probably areas of DNA. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A round Petri dish with a green bacterial lawn and five small white antibiotic discs. Three discs on the left and upper right have large clear circular zones around them with no bacterial growth. One disc at lower right has a medium clear zone. The two discs at lower left and bottom centre have no clear zone, and bacteria grow right up to them. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained blood smear viewed under a microscope, with many pink-red biconcave red blood cells. Three white blood cells are among them: a large one on the left with a kidney-shaped, pale purple nucleus, a middle one with a lobed, irregular purple nucleus, and a small one on the right with a dark, round, densely stained nucleus. A small cluster of platelets is at the bottom. There are no labels.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour electron micrograph of a single cell in section. A large nucleus, brown with green patches, sits at the top, slightly right of centre. The rest of the cell is filled with teal cytoplasm containing many concentric layers of membrane, a few darker blue organelles and small black dots. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A green wire-mesh molecular model of an antibody, Y-shaped, with two arms and a stem against a black background. A small red mesh blob, an antigen, is bound to the tip of the right arm, and a small yellow patch marks the contact point. No labels are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A colour photograph of an adult and a child sitting close together, both facing the camera. The faces and bare upper bodies of both are covered with raised, round pustular lesions, a rash typical of a viral skin infection such as smallpox. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of the face and upper shoulders of a young dark-skinned person against a blue background. The eyelids are drooping and half closed, the eyes look downward, and the face looks swollen and puffy around the eyes. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour electron micrograph of muscle tissue. Many rounded mitochondria with green outlines and closely spaced parallel internal folds (cristae) are packed in columns between pink striated myofibril bands. Each myofibril has dark red transverse lines at regular intervals. Orange-red granular material lies between the structures. There are no labels or scale.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A drawing of apparatus on a retort stand: a clamp holds a thermometer in a beaker of water, with a test tube tilted in the water. To the right are a beaker full of ice cubes and an electric kettle. The thermometer scale is marked in °C from 0 to 100, and the red liquid column is at about 10 °C.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of plant root tip cells stained green-blue, in which each rectangular cell has a thick cell wall and a dark-stained, roughly round nucleus. The cells are arranged in columns. One cell at lower left has a less distinct, more irregular dark mass of chromatin. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through a plant structure, stained blue. A small central vascular bundle with a ring of reddish-purple cells is surrounded by a wide cortex of rounded cells. Several large irregular air spaces lie in the cortex, and an outer layer of small cells forms the edge. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of part of a transverse section of a plant stem. The epidermis is a single outer layer, with small thick-walled cells (sclerenchyma/collenchyma) beneath it. Below these are large pale parenchyma cells containing three vascular bundles. The bundles are stained magenta and blue-green, and the central one is the largest. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour electron micrograph of part of a muscle cell in longitudinal section. Pink myofibril bundles with dark red transverse lines run vertically. Between them are columns of rounded mitochondria with green outlines and blue-pink interiors showing many fine parallel cristae, surrounded by orange-red granular cytoplasm. There are no labels and no scale.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a large, round egg cell (oocyte) with a granular cytoplasm, surrounded by a clear zona pellucida and a few small debris particles. On the right, a thick holding pipette holds the cell by suction. On the left, a thin injection needle points toward the cell. The image has no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black-and-white electron micrograph of a single elongated, oval mitochondrion in longitudinal section. It has a double outer membrane and many inner folds (cristae) running across the matrix, with small dark granules in the matrix. Layers of rough endoplasmic reticulum lie beneath it and dark vesicles lie above it. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through a rice root, stained blue-green on a cream background. The centre has a small stele with vascular tissue. Around it is a wide cortex with many large air spaces (aerenchyma) separated by thin strands of cells, and an outer layer of cells at the edge. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of flooded rice paddies. Young rice seedlings grow in shallow standing water in the foreground, and brighter green seedlings form a denser patch beyond. Separate fields are divided by low earth banks, with taller green rice fields, trees and hills in the background. No labels or values are printed.
figures.original: Adaptations of rice for wet environments Although rice can grow in dry conditions, it is often grown in ‘paddies’ – fields where the ground is intentionally flooded. Rice can tolerate

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of several long, parallel transparent tubes filled with bright green liquid, with water droplets on their surfaces. The tubes end in dark grey curved elbow joints with bolted flanges, and they sit on a dark ground marked with pale lines. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black-and-white transmission electron micrograph of a single chloroplast in section, roughly oval, surrounded by an envelope. Inside the granular stroma are many stacks of closely packed thylakoid membranes (grana) joined by longer membranes running between them. One pale oval body, probably a starch grain, lies at the right. A few small dark dots are scattered in the stroma. No labels or scale bar are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a photosynthometer set-up. A boiling tube holds dark green aquatic plant material in a clear stand. A thin tube leads from the top of the boiling tube to a horizontal capillary tube lying along a ruler. The capillary tube connects by a curved flexible tube to a syringe, and the ruler and syringe are mounted on a green board. A young man in a white lab coat sits behind the apparatus and looks at it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained light micrograph of a transverse section through a leaf. Several vascular bundles are surrounded by rings of cells stained red and green, and large, clear, thin-walled cells lie between the bundles. The upper and lower epidermis are visible, with small hairs on the upper surface. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black bear walks through shallow, fast-flowing water over rocks. It holds a silvery fish, a salmon, in its mouth, and water splashes around its face. Mossy rocks and a rock wall are in the background. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained light micrograph of a section of kidney cortex. A large glomerulus, a tuft of capillaries stained blue with red and purple nuclei, sits in the centre inside a clear Bowman's capsule space. Cross-sections of kidney tubules surround it. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A pink-stained light micrograph of kidney tissue in section, packed with many round and oval tubule cross-sections. Each has a ring of cuboidal cells with dark purple nuclei around a central pale lumen. Small red-stained clusters of red blood cells lie in the spaces between the tubules. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph of a glomerulus in the kidney. Rounded capillary loops are covered in teal-blue podocytes, whose foot-like processes (pedicels) interdigitate across the purple-pink capillary surface. There are no labels, numbers or scale bar.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A line graph with a logarithmic y-axis from 0.01 to 100, labelled 'Concentration / number of times greater than the concentration in the blood plasma'. The x-axis is divided into four regions: proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct. Urea rises from 1 to about 60. Glucose and amino acids fall steeply from 1 to 0.01 in the proximal tubule. K+ stays at 1, rises to about 2, drops to about 0.3, then climbs to about 11. Na+ stays at 1, drops to about 0.3, then rises to about 0.9.
labels: Concentration / number of times greater than the concentration in the blood plasma

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A diagram of negative feedback control of blood glucose. A green wavy line shows blood glucose concentration moving above and below a shaded green band marked as the usual range, with a dashed line through the middle. At the top, a Receptors box leads by a blue arrow ("less glucagon and more insulin secreted") to an Effectors box, and a red arrow points to the falling part of the curve. At the bottom, a Receptors box leads by a blue arrow ("more glucagon less insulin") to an Effectors box, and a red arrow points to the rising part of the curve.
labels: Negative feedback control of high blood glucose concentration
α and β cells in the islets of Langerhans detect rise in blood glucose.
less glucagon and more insulin secreted
Liver cells respond to less glucagon – no glycogen breakdown.
Liver, muscle and fat cells respond to more insulin – increased uptake and use of glucose.
α and β cells in the islets detect fall in blood glucose.
Liver cells respond to more glucagon by breaking down glycogen into glucose.
Liver, muscle and fat cells respond to less insulin – reduced uptake of glucose.
Negative feedback control of low blood glucose concentration

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black and white electron micrograph of part of a cell. Stacks of flattened, parallel membrane-bound cisternae (rough endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi-like) curve alongside the nuclear envelope, with the nucleus on the right showing pale chromatin and dark clumps. Several round to oval mitochondria and dark granular clusters (likely glycogen or ribosomes) lie in the cytoplasm. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A gloved hand holds a FreeStyle Freedom Lite blood glucose meter. A test strip is inserted in the meter, and its tip touches a drop of blood on a fingertip. The screen reads 5.9 with the unit mmol/L and the small text 16-09 07.11. The meter has two buttons marked m and c.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through a leaf, stained blue. A thin epidermis lies at the top and bottom. Below the upper epidermis are elongated palisade cells in two layers. Beneath them is spongy mesophyll with rounded cells and air spaces, and two vascular bundles are visible in the middle. A small gap, probably a stoma, lies in the lower epidermis. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of leaf epidermis showing two stomata, each with a central slit-like pore between two guard cells. Small round chloroplasts are visible inside the guard cells. The surrounding epidermal cells have wavy, interlocking outlines. No labels or scale are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black and white photomicrograph of kidney tissue. On the right is a glomerulus, a dense ball of dark-stained cells inside a rounded capsule with a pale space around it. Around it are many sections of tubules, each with a ring of cells with dark nuclei surrounding a pale central lumen. No labels or scale are visible.
figures.original: b The figure is a photomicrograph of part of the kidney.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A view of a human body from behind, with the brain visible through the top of the head and the spinal cord running down the middle of the back. Many yellow nerves branch off the spinal cord on both sides and spread out across the back, shoulders and buttocks. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph in blue-green of a star-shaped cell with several branching extensions, probably a neurone cell body. It has a central rounded region with a ring-like rim and a rough, textured surface, and it lies among similar web-like cells against dark gaps. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a transverse section through a nerve, with many myelinated axons cut across. Each appears as a round pale centre surrounded by a thick dark ring of myelin, with smaller pink-stained connective tissue between them. A pink-stained connective tissue sheath (perineurium) curves along the left side and encloses the bundle. No labels or scale are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour transmission electron micrograph of a synapse between two neurone endings, with no labels. The lower-right ending is packed with small blue vesicles and contains an elongated green mitochondrion. The upper-left ending is larger and contains a green mitochondrion but no vesicles. A thin blue gap separates the two endings. Another green mitochondrion is visible in a neighbouring profile at top left.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of stained skeletal muscle fibres with clear cross-striations. Thin nerve fibres run across the muscle fibres and end at dark, granular patches on the fibre surfaces, which look like neuromuscular junctions. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of striated muscle fibres stained pink/red with fine, regular transverse stripes running across the fibres. A pale gap between two fibres runs vertically down the centre and contains blue-stained connective tissue and a small ring-shaped structure, probably a capillary or a nucleus. There are no labels or scale bar.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A coloured electron micrograph of a longitudinal section of striated muscle. It shows repeating sarcomere bands in blue, green and purple, dark vertical Z lines, and a lighter central line in each sarcomere. Rows of mitochondria with purple-outlined membranes lie between the myofibrils. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A sarcomere is drawn with a central thick filament that has myosin heads projecting along its length. Thin filaments lie above and below, entering from the left and right, with pink arrows pointing toward the centre. A boxed region on the right is enlarged in two panels. The first shows a myosin head attached to the thin filament, bending with an arrow pointing left. The second shows the myosin head detached and in a different position. There are no text labels.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A drawing of the female reproductive system seen from the front. It shows the uterus with a thick, speckled lining, the cervix and vagina below it, and a fallopian tube curving up to one ovary on the right. The ovary is a yellow oval with a single small follicle containing an oocyte. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An unlabelled drawing of the female reproductive system seen from the front: the uterus with a thick lining, two oviducts, and the vagina and cervix at the bottom. An ovary on the right side is shown as a yellowish mass containing a large follicle with an oocyte and smaller structures, with the oviduct curving over it. No text or numbers are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a Venus flytrap leaf trap with a dark fly caught between its two lobes. The fly's wings and body stick out of the trap, and the marginal spikes (teeth) along the lobe edges interlock around it. Green moss surrounds the trap. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two diagrams of a sarcomere with horizontal filaments. In the top one, thick black filaments lie in the middle with a vertical line through their centre, and thinner grey filaments extend in from the left and right, each side attached to a vertical grey line, with a gap between the grey and black filaments. In the bottom one, the grey filaments overlap the ends of the black filaments, and small arrows on the black filaments point toward the centre on both sides. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two schematic diagrams of a sarcomere-like arrangement, one above the other, with no printed labels. Each has a central vertical black line with thick black horizontal filaments (with small angled barbs, myosin-like) and thin grey horizontal filaments attached to grey vertical lines at the left and right ends. In the upper diagram the grey filaments stop short of the centre, leaving a wide gap. In the lower diagram the grey filaments reach almost to the centre and overlap the black filaments more, leaving only a small gap.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two patterns of black dots arranged in roughly hexagonal or circular arrays, side by side. The left pattern has smaller dots that are more closely spaced. The right pattern has larger dots in rows of 3, 4, 5, 4 and 3, giving 19 dots, and the dots are more widely spaced. There are no labels or values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a bright pink katydid (an oblong-winged katydid) standing on a green leaf, seen from the side. It has long thin antennae, long legs and a large wing covering its body, with a blurred green background. There are no labels or printed values.
figures.original: Oblong-winged katydids are normally green and well camouflaged. Occasionally, a bright pink katydid occurs (Figure 16.1). The pink colour is caused by an allele (variety) of the gene that determines body col

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black-and-white karyotype of human chromosomes arranged in homologous pairs numbered 1 to 22, plus X and Y. The groups are bracketed and labelled: A (1–3), B (4–5), C (6–12), D (13–15), E (16–18), F (19–20), G (21–22). The sex chromosomes X and Y are shown at the bottom right, with X large and Y small.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a single rounded cell, apparently an egg cell (secondary oocyte), with a granular cytoplasm. It is surrounded by a thin clear ring, probably the zona pellucida, against a blue background. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a single, round, mammalian egg cell (oocyte) on a blue background. The cell has a granular-looking cytoplasm and a clear, thin outline around it. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a cell that has divided into two daughter cells, seen as two rounded cells joined together in a figure-of-eight shape on a blue background. Each cell has a visible nucleus-like region near its centre. No labels, scale bar or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with a yellow-orange background showing a large cell with two groups of dark, stained chromosomes. One group is at the lower left and the other at the upper right, with the groups well separated. Each group is a rosette of short, thick, arm-like chromosomes. No labels or scale values are printed on the image.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a single animal cell (locust) on an orange-yellow background, with a faint cell outline. Dark, rod-shaped chromosomes are clustered near the centre of the cell, and no labels are printed on it.
figures.original: Figure 16.9 Stages of meiosis in an animal cell (locust) (× 950). Interphase (not part of meiosis) is also shown. 16.2 Name the stage of meiosis at which each of the following occurs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with a yellow-orange background showing a cell with about a dozen dark, stained chromosomes of different sizes. Most are clustered in a loose group on the left, and one more lies separately to the right. No labels or scale bar are printed on it.
figures.original: Figure 16.9 Stages of meiosis in an animal cell (locust) (× 950). Interphase (not part of meiosis) is also shown. 16.2 Name the stage of meiosis at which each of the following occurs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with an orange-yellow background showing two separate groups of dark, stained chromosomes, one on the left and one on the right. Each group contains many small rod-shaped and V-shaped chromosomes. The two groups lie at opposite sides of one cell, as in late anaphase or telophase of meiosis. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with an orange-yellow background showing a single cell with dark, thread-like condensed chromosomes of varying lengths and shapes. They are clustered together in the middle of the cell, and some look like X-shapes or rings. A faint, grainy nucleus is partly visible at the top left corner. There are no labels or printed values.
figures.original: Figure 16.9 Stages of meiosis in an animal cell (locust) (× 950). Interphase (not part of meiosis) is also shown. 16.2 Name the stage of meiosis at which each of the following occurs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a single cell nucleus on an orange-yellow background. Thin, dark, beaded thread-like chromosomes are tangled together in a roughly round mass. No labels or scale values are printed on the image.
figures.original: Figure 16.9 Stages of meiosis in an animal cell (locust) (× 950). Interphase (not part of meiosis) is also shown. 16.2 Name the stage of meiosis at which each of the following occurs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with an orange-yellow background shows two separate groups of dark, rod-shaped chromosomes. One group is on the left and one is on the right, and each group has about 10 to 12 chromosomes of varying lengths. A faint cell outline surrounds both groups, and a few small dots lie between them. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with an orange-yellow background showing a single cell in which dark, rod-shaped chromosomes are scattered in a ring-like arrangement. The chromosomes appear as short, thick dark bodies, and some seem paired or split. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.
figures.original: Figure 16.9 Stages of meiosis in an animal cell (locust) (× 950). Interphase (not part of meiosis) is also shown. 16.2 Name the stage of meiosis at which each of the following occurs.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A coloured scanning electron micrograph of six roughly spherical yellow-gold pollen grains on a black background. Each grain has a surface covered in small pointed spines and bumps. No labels, scale bar or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a white rabbit with pink-red eyes and pink inner ears, sitting on dark brown soil with a few dry leaves. It is seen from the side and has no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a wild rabbit sitting on short grass, seen from the side and facing left. It has light brown-grey fur, long upright ears, a dark eye and a short tail. Green leafy plants are in the background. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a white rabbit sitting on short green grass, seen from the side. Its ears, nose and feet are dark (black), and its eye is red or pink. This is the Himalayan colour pattern. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a grey rabbit with a white tail, sitting on its hind legs and grooming itself with its front paws raised to its face. The background is plain blue. The coat is grey with darker markings on the ears, legs and face. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two line drawings of Drosophila appendages, both covered in fine hairs. The upper left one is a short, oval, hairy antenna with a long feathery bristle (arista) and a few bristles at the base. The lower right one is a longer, segmented, leg-like antenna with a swollen section and a narrow, jointed end, with bristles at the base. A scale bar is labelled 0.1mm.
figures.original: A recessive allele for antennal shape, called ‘aristopedia’, gives an antenna looking rather like a Drosophila leg, with two claws

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black-and-white micrograph of chromosomes spread on a pale background. Several are ring-shaped, some are rod-like or curved dark bands, and a few have a pale looped or open outline with dark spots. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two circles, each representing a nucleus containing chromosomes drawn as rounded rods. The left circle has six chromosomes with no pattern labels: three plain grey and three black-and-white speckled. The right circle has the same six chromosomes shaded differently: one long dotted hooked chromosome and one shorter dotted hooked chromosome, two cross-hatched long chromosomes, and two small diagonal-hatched chromosomes. Two of the chromosomes are long and hooked, two are long and straight, and two are short. No text labels are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a single fly orchid flower (Ophrys insectifera) on a green stem. It has narrow green sepals spreading sideways, a green sepal above, and two thin dark antenna-like petals. The dark reddish-brown velvety labellum has a pale bluish-white central patch, so the flower looks like a small insect. No labels are printed.
figures.original: Coevolution is the evolution of the adaptations of two species as a result of the selective pressures each exerts on the other. This has occurred in the adaptations of the flowers of various species o

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A Siamese cat sits against a plain blue background with one front paw raised. Its body is pale cream, and its ears, face mask, legs, paws and tail are dark brown. Its eyes are blue. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black and white photograph of a snow-covered field with a very large number of hares or rabbits running and sitting among low bushes. A barbed wire fence with wooden posts crosses the foreground. In the background several people on horseback are spread across the field, and a wooden enclosure stands at the upper left. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a wild rabbit lying on grass beside orange-brown bracken fronds. The rabbit's eyelids look swollen and closed, and the eye area is pink and inflamed, which are signs of myxomatosis. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A white hare with black-tipped ears sits upright on snow, seen from the side and facing right. The snow around it is smooth and bluish, and the hare's white coat blends in with it. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A colour photograph of a tuatara, a lizard-like reptile with a spiny crest along its back, resting on a dark rock. Green leaves are in the background. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Several Petri dishes with an orange-red agar background are photographed against a dark background. Each dish has small white paper discs. Some discs are surrounded by dark circular clear zones of different sizes, and other discs have no zone around them. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A dark, melanic peppered moth with its wings spread rests on a patch of white, peeling birch bark. The surrounding bark is darker brown. The moth's body is dark and furry, and it contrasts strongly with the pale bark. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a dark, almost black moth resting on rough brown bark with its wings spread. The moth has a dark body and dark wings, and it is fairly conspicuous against the lighter, mottled bark. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A stained blood smear seen through a light microscope. It shows many pale pinkish-brown red blood cells and two white blood cells with purple-stained nuclei. The white cell on the left has blue cytoplasm and a rounded nucleus. The white cell on the right has a pale cytoplasm and an elongated, folded nucleus. A few red cells contain small dark spots, and a small purple platelet is near the top. No labels or printed values are visible.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a herd of about fifteen reddish-brown cows with white patches on the legs and underside. They walk across a sparse grassy field toward the viewer. Scrub, trees and a low stone wall are in the background under a blue sky. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a white adult cow with two curved horns and dark markings on its face and legs, walking to the left across grass. A small white calf walks behind it, to the right. The calf has no visible horns. The background is grassland. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A map of the Middle East with water in pale blue and land in beige. A green crescent-shaped region curves from the eastern Mediterranean coast round the north of the Arabian desert to the head of the Persian Gulf, with a narrower green strip running south along the Mediterranean coast. Blue lines mark rivers, including two that run south-east through the green area to the Gulf, and a river further south-west. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A black and white photograph of eight maize plants standing in a row against a plain pale wall. The plants differ in height: the tallest are on the left and the shorter ones are towards the middle and right. Each has long strap-shaped leaves and a tassel at the top. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a field of tall maize (corn) plants against a blue sky with thin clouds. The plants have broad, strap-shaped green leaves, and feathery male flowers (tassels) stand at the tops of the stems. There are no labels or printed values.
figures.original: Maize, Zea mays, is also known as corn in some parts of the world. It is a sturdy, tall grass with broad, strap- shaped leaves (Figure 17.21).

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a single red flower hanging beneath green leaves. It has five narrow, twisted red petals and a long central column with pale yellow anthers and a red-pink stigma. A pale green bud sits above the flower, and further buds are visible among the leaves. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An underwater photograph of a feather duster (fan) worm with a circular fan of brownish, cream-banded feathery tentacles at the centre. Around it are several sea urchins with long dark and orange spines, a red sponge on the right and yellowish encrusting growth in the background. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a salt marsh with dense, tall yellow-green cord grass in the foreground and middle ground. Dark mud and flattened dry grass lie on the right, with a dark rock or object near the lower right. Bare and leafy trees line the horizon under a clear blue sky. There is no printed text.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A slug with a dark black-brown body covered in white or cream spots and blotches, crawling over bright green moss. It has two long tentacles at the head end, a saddle-shaped mantle behind the head, and a pale grey underside and foot. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a mockingbird perched on a weathered, lichen-covered branch, seen from the front and slightly to the side, with a blurred green and brown background. The bird has a long, slightly downcurved dark beak, a pale white underside, dark streaks and blotches on the breast, dark mottled brown wings, a long tail with pale tips, and long dark legs with strong claws gripping the branch. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a moss-covered tree branch in a rainforest. An epiphytic bromeliad with long green leaves and a small orange-red flower grows on the branch, and thick green moss and other plants surround it. Broad green leaves fill the background. No labels are printed.
figures.original: A habitat describes the place where a species lives within an ecosystem. The niche occupied by a species is more than a physical description of a place.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A white egret with a long neck and an orange-yellow beak stands in shallow water. It holds a small fish crosswise in its beak. Its reflection shows on the calm water surface, and clumps of grass and reeds grow at the left edge.
figures.original: A habitat describes the place where a species lives within an ecosystem. The niche occupied by a species is more than a physical description of a place. A niche is the role of an

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a dark greenish-brown reptile, a tuatara, seen from the side on soil and leaf litter. It has a spiny crest along the neck and back, small rough granular scales, pale spots on the throat, and clawed toes. The background is blurred. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a tropical ecosystem. Dense, overgrown grass and shrubs fill the foreground and middle. Several coconut palms and other trees stand in the background against a pale sky. A small pile of rubble and a piece of white litter lie at the bottom of the frame. There are no labels.
figures.original: Imagine you are in an ecosystem like that in Figure 18.6. The most obvious species are the larg

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A man in a utility vest with climbing ropes and harness attached sucks on a clear tube while a second bent yellow tube points into a mound of moss. The setup looks like a pooter (aspirator) used to collect small invertebrates from the moss. He is in a green, leafy forest setting. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a pile of about ten snails on a white background. The shells differ in colour and banding: plain yellow, pale cream-green, yellow with dark brown stripes, and orange-brown with dark and white bands. Some snails show their bodies and tentacles. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A drawing of a grassland area with broad-leaved plants among grasses. A white measuring tape is laid along two sides of a square sampling area, with a black dashed line marking the other two sides. A red square, a smaller quadrat, is drawn inside the area. Small numbers are printed along the tape, and the corner is marked 0.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Two students crouch on a grassy lawn beside a square quadrat frame that is strung with a grid of thin lines dividing it into smaller squares. A long tape or line runs across the grass beside the quadrat. One student points at plants inside the quadrat, which holds a few small weeds and two yellow dandelion flowers. The other student holds a notebook or book. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An underwater photograph of a red sea anemone with many tentacles spreading upward and outward. It is attached to a rock with a pink encrusting growth, and other organisms are around it. The background is blue and out of focus. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph with a green tint showing long, curved chains of rounded cells, like strings of beads, which look like the cyanobacterium Nostoc. Most cells are small and granular. A few larger, paler, thick-walled cells with clear contents sit within the chains. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An underwater photograph of a deep-sea hydrothermal vent, a black smoker, with a dark plume of mineral-rich fluid rising on the right. The vent surface is covered in white and red tube worms. Research equipment is visible: a cylindrical sampling instrument with a yellow cable at the upper left, and more apparatus at the lower right. The surrounding water is dark blue. No labels are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A false-colour scanning electron micrograph with orange rounded cells on a green-teal granular background. Thin yellow threads (filaments) spread from and between the cells. Two cells in the centre are joined by a thicker tube-like bridge, and some cells look folded or divided. There are no labels, scale bar or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a single large, elongated, trumpet-shaped ciliate protozoan, wider at the top and narrowing to a tail at the bottom. The top edge has a fringe of long cilia. The cytoplasm contains several rounded food vacuoles, some coloured yellow, orange or green. No labels, scale bar or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: Four pale brown puffball fungi of different heights stand on dry grass and bracken against a black background. A cloud of white smoke-like spores rises from the top of the second fungus from the right. No labels or values are printed on it.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A light micrograph of a Volvox colony: a large spherical colony with a ring of tiny green cells around its edge. Inside are about eight larger, oval, bright green daughter colonies. Some daughter colonies show a fine dotted pattern of cells. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of an old, gnarled tree with twisted, spiralling, pale orange-brown wood and bare, dead-looking branches. It stands on a rocky slope of loose pale stones against a deep blue sky. Dark green foliage is visible on the left, and smaller trees and distant hills are in the background. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of tree ferns growing in a dense forest. Several upright, fibrous brown trunks each carry a spreading crown of large, finely divided green fronds. Smaller ferns and other vegetation fill the background and foreground. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An underwater photograph of a crown-of-thorns starfish (a spiny, many-armed echinoderm) resting on pink and white coral reef. Its arms are covered in long, sharp, dark spines with pale bases. Small fish swim in the blue water above and behind it. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A 3D rendered model of a cylindrical helical structure, resembling a virus particle such as tobacco mosaic virus. It is built from many repeating beige or grey subunits arranged in a spiral around a central hollow core. One ring of subunits at the top is coloured blue. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of young tobacco plants growing in bare brown soil. Several large green leaves have yellow and brown patches and spots, mostly on the leaves on the right. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: An underwater photograph looking up through a kelp forest. Tall kelp fronds with broad yellow-green blades are lit by sunlight from the surface, with blue water behind them. Several small fish swim among the fronds. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A sea otter floats on its back in blue water with its pale head raised and one dark hind flipper sticking up out of the water. Pieces of brown kelp float on the surface around it. There are no labels or printed values.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A photograph of a young giant panda cub facing the camera, sitting behind a wooden log with one front paw resting on it. It has a white face and body, black ears, black eye patches, a black nose, and black legs and shoulders. The background is blurred blue-green. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A close-up photograph of a primate with bright orange-gold fur, a greyish bare face and brown eyes. It is gripping a branch at the lower left, and the background is blurred grey. It looks like a golden lion tamarin. No labels or values are printed.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology Coursebook
figures.shows: A person in a dark hooded coat with a face covering holds up a large glass jar full of seeds, in a storage room. Behind them are shelves holding many rows of sealed jars, each with a white label. The labels are too small to read.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge IGCSE® English as a Second Language Coursebook
figures.shows: A screenshot of an email in an inbox window titled 'Re: Update — Inbox'. The header has blank From and To fields, the subject 'Re: Update' and the date '15 April 2014 18:09:49'. The body is a letter to the editor from 'A worried listener' who objects to a young man's opinion on written versus spoken English. The letter says correct spoken language gives a good first impression and that decent spoken English is essential in the job market.
labels: I have just been listening online to a young man talking about the differences between written and spoken English. I am writing to you to let you know that I think his opinion is a great cause for concern.

It is crucial that everyone is able to speak English to an effective level, and saying that 'it's OK' to make fundamental grammar mistakes is just ridiculous! Correct spoken language gives a good first impression, and I am sure that the vast majority of people would agree with me. Certainly in the job market, decent spoken English is essential.
I hope that other readers will agree with me that we should be concerned about this downgrading of spoken language.
figures.original: What information is given in the email? Match parts of the e-mail with the information a-f.

figures.textbookName: Cambridge IGCSE® English as a Second Language Coursebook
figures.shows: A handwritten-style informal letter addressed 'Dear ESS', dated January 29, from a student named Bruno asking for information about spelling courses. It has two paragraphs and is signed 'Best wishes Bruno'. The text contains spelling and grammar errors such as 'cources', 'speling', 'studyng', 'prizes', 'lenth' and 'informations'.
labels: I have seen your advertisement today in my local newspaper magazine and want to get more information from you about the cources you offer people who want to improve their speling. I would like to be able to throw away your dictionary and not worry any more about making speing mistakes. I would like to help your friends and work colleagues with their speling.

I am a student who I am studyng english in college and my speling is not very good so I want to improve and write better english. I need to write compositions in english and I do not have time to use a dictionary all the time at home and at school. Please will you send me some informations about your cources, the prizes and lenth and the materials you will send me and tell me when I can start a cource with ESS. I am look forward to hear from you a.s.a.p.
figures.original: Look at this letter written by a student in response to the question in Activity E8. The writer of this letter has made some language mistakes. figures.shows: A cross-section diagram titled 'Converging and diverging plates' showing crust and mantle. On the left, a convergent (destructive) plate boundary has a continental plate with a strato-volcano and fold mountains, and an oceanic plate subducting beneath it to form a trench. On the right, a divergent (constructive) plate boundary has two plates pulling apart under the ocean at a ridge with a shield volcano, a hot spot, and convection currents in the mantle. Text boxes describe a 'crust bin' and a 'crust factory', continental and oceanic plates, and plate movement of about 40 mm per year with a range of 10 to 180 mm.

Horizontal layers of sedimentary rock are squeezed up into fold mountains
Shape of junction is a trench
Plates pulling apart can cause earthquakes at ridges
Edges of plates pushed up by convection currents to form ridges
Oceanic crust (heavy) sinks beneath continental crust (light) and melts, creating heat and pressure and magma (molten rock)
Continental plate – this part of a plate is mostly above the ocean, forming land. It is between 25 and 100 km thick and is mostly made of granite, a lighter rock than basalt.
Oceanic plate – this part of a plate is mostly below the ocean. It is mainly made of basalt between 5 and 10 km thick. It is a dense, heavy rock so it sinks below the continental plates.
New crust as magma cools from mantle
Sea floor spreads as plates move apart or diverge
Plates are moving very slowly. The average movement is about 40 mm per year with a range of 10 mm to 180 mm estimated – but over a million years this can amount to a great distance in kilometres.

Divergent: Spreading; Constructive – new crust created, a crust 'factory'; Ridge; Earthquakes and shield volcanoes. Conservative: The plates slide sideways by each other; Crust neither created nor destroyed; No major effect; Earthquakes.

It says landfall will be near 20.6°S 56.5°E with winds around 166 km/h, and that a category 2 storm on the Saffir-Simpson scale damages roofing, doors, windows, shrubbery, trees, mobile homes, signs and piers. labels: Mauritius: tropical storm Bejisa is forecast to strike Mauritius as a tropical cyclone at about 06.00 on 3 January 2014
Data supplied by the US Navy and Air Force Joint Typhoon Warning Center suggests that the point of landfall will be near 20.6°S 56.5°E.
Bejisa is expected to bring winds of around 166 km/h with gusts that may be considerably higher.

According to the Saffir-Simpson scale, the damage from a storm of Bejisa's strength (category 2) includes damage to roofing material, doors and windows, damage to shrubbery and trees with some trees blown down and considerable damage to mobile homes, poorly constructed signs, and piers.

Small craft in unprotected anchorages may break their moorings and coastal and low-lying areas are likely to flood two to four hours before the arrival of the storm centre as sea level will rise by between 1.8 and 2.4 metres.
figures.original: Make a list of the likely impacts of a tropical storm on the coast of Mauritius.

figures.shows: A timeline titled 'A The development of the Nokia corporation' lists dated entries from 1865 to 2014. The entries run: 1865 wood pulp mill, 1898 Finnish Rubber Works, 1912 Finnish Cable Works, 1962 electronics, 1963 radio telephones, 1982 first car phone and digital telephone, 1987 first handheld mobile phone, 1998 world leader in mobile phones, 2005 billionth phone sold in Nigeria, 2014 Microsoft acquired Nokia's devices and services business.
labels: The development of the Nokia corporation

Mining engineer Fredrik Idestam set up his first wood pulp mill at the Tammerkoski Rapids in south-western Finland. A few years later he opened a second mill on the banks of the Nokianvirta river after which the company was named 'Nokia Ab'.
The Finnish Rubber Works was set up, which later became Nokia's rubber business, making everything from rubber boots to tyres.
The Finnish Cable Works was established, the start of Nokia's cable and electronics business.
The Finnish Cable Works started branching out into electronics. It made an electronic device for use in nuclear power plants.
It started developing radio telephones for the army and emergency services.
Nokia introduced the first car phone and digital telephone.
Nokia introduced the first handheld mobile phone.
Nokia was the world leader in mobile phones.
Nokia sold its billionth phone – in Nigeria.
Microsoft acquired Nokia's devices and services business.
figures.original: Write a paragraph which describes how Nokia developed from a small company to a transnational corporation.

figures.shows: A world map titled 'Nokia worldwide' with countries where Nokia operates shaded yellow. Text boxes with arrows give the location, year established and details for Hungary, Mexico, Brazil, India, China (Dongguan and Beijing), South Korea and Vietnam. labels: The factory has a workforce that is 70% female. In and around the town Nokia supports the local hospital, fire department and schools. They also built a by-pass road to the Nokia site, helping reduce traffic congestion and lower emissions.

Around 98% of the workforce comes from the local area and the factory supports the local university, schools, orphanages and shelters. Situated just a few miles from the US border, Reynosa delivers smartphones to North, Central and South America.
Nokia also established the Nokia Foundation, a technical high school with 450 students.

Chennai, one of Nokia's biggest factories, received the Golden Peacock Award for its high standards of environment management in 2010. It is also active in the community with projects ranging from a local library programme to village regeneration projects.
The Dongguan factory produces almost a third of Nokia's entire mobile phone output.
In the XingWang industrial park Nokia is linked with several suppliers, helping to reduce transportation costs and save on energy.
At Masan, new state-of-the-art facilities were opened in 2012. The local community supplies almost 99% of Nokia's workforce, 68% of whom are women.
The new US$302 million factory covers a total area of 65 400 m² and is located in the Vietnam–Singapore Industrial Zone.
